meta.source: Integrated Farming System content blueprint for the BKS website, 18 Aug 2026

h1: What is an Integrated Farming System (IFS)?
lede: An Integrated Farming System (IFS) is a holistic, circular agricultural model where multiple agricultural enterprises—such as crop cultivation, horticulture, dairy, poultry, aquaculture, agroforestry, and beekeeping—are combined on a single piece of land. In a traditional monoculture setup, a farmer relies on one single crop (like paddy) and bears huge market, weather, and input risks. In an Integrated Farming System, the waste or by-product of one component becomes the direct, free input for another. This closed-loop system slashes external input costs, maximizes soil vitality, optimizes water use, and generates multiple, steady streams of daily, monthly, and seasonal income.
photoCap: Durga Puja Mahotsav 2025, IIT Kharagpur Research Park — KarmYog for the 21st Century Foundation.

what.body: One standing crop carries the whole year’s risk. An integrated farm turns leftover into input — so work, water and cash move through the year.

contrast.title: Single crop
contrast.body: One standing crop, often paddy. Market, weather and bought inputs hit the whole year at once.

contrast.title: Integrated loop
contrast.body: Several enterprises on the same land. One leftover becomes the next free input. Daily, monthly and seasonal income together.

need.h2: Why West Bengal Urgently Needs IFS
need.intro: West Bengal is one of the most biologically fertile regions in the world, blessed with rich alluvial soil, abundant groundwater, and varied agro-climatic zones. However, the state’s agrarian economy faces several structural bottlenecks:

items.title: Extreme Land Fragmentation
items.body: Most farmers in Bengal are small and marginal landholders, often on less than 1 hectare. Single-crop farming on tiny parcels simply cannot sustain a modern rural household.

items.title: High Input Costs & Low Margins
items.body: Heavy dependence on commercial chemical fertilizers, hybrid seeds, and pesticides eats away farmer margins and degrades long-term soil fertility.

items.title: Climate & Flood Vulnerabilities
items.body: Monsoonal flooding, cyclone impacts, and delayed rains frequently wipe out single standing crops.

items.title: Seasonality of Cash Flow
items.body: Monoculture leaves farmers cash-poor between harvesting seasons, pushing them into vicious debt cycles with middlemen.

need.outro: The Integrated Farming System directly solves these vulnerabilities by maximizing the productivity per square meter of small land parcels, insulating farmers from market price crashes, and restoring natural soil resilience.

pillars.h2: The Core Modules of a Bengal Model Integrated Farm
pillars.intro: An illustrative BKS model integrated farm (sketched for about 1 to 2.5 acre holdings) is structured around five symbiotic pillars. Mix, scale and results vary.

items.title: Aquaculture & Water Harvesting (The Central Engine)
items.body: At the heart of the farm lies a well-engineered pond. It serves as both a rainwater harvesting reservoir and a high-yield fishery for native carps (Rohu, Katla, Mrigal) and high-value indigenous fish. The pond water is naturally enriched with nutrients, making it ideal for gravity-fed micro-irrigation.

items.title: Bund & Embankment Multi-Tier Horticulture
items.body: The raised bunds (dykes) surrounding the pond are never left idle. They are planted in three vertical tiers. Canopy Tier: Coconut, Betel nut (Supari), Drumstick (Sajna), and Papaya. Climbing Tier: Trellises built over the pond edge for bottle gourd (Lau), bitter gourd (Karela), and pointed gourd (Potol). Ground Tier: High-value turmeric, ginger, and seasonal green leafy vegetables.

items.title: Livestock & Poultry Integration
items.body: Directly adjacent to or cantilevered over the farm pond, small-scale dairy units (2–4 indigenous or crossbred cows) and poultry/duckery sheds are installed. Duck-Fish Symbiosis: Ducks forage on aquatic weeds and insects while their droppings drop directly into the pond as natural plankton feed. Cow Dung & Bio-Gas: Cow dung and urine fuel an on-site mini-biogas unit (providing domestic cooking fuel and lighting) and produce rich bio-slurry for composting.

items.title: Bio-inputs and soil regeneration
items.body: No crop residue or animal waste leaves the farm. Through vermicomposting beds, Jeevamrutha preparation tanks, and biochar pits, farm biomass is converted directly into organic compost, eliminating the need for expensive chemical fertilizers.

items.title: Smart Technology & Precision Monitoring (AI-Enabled)
items.body: Integrating 21st-century technology into traditional agriculture: soil moisture sensors and automated drip irrigation; solar-powered aeration for fish ponds; real-time digital crop health diagnostics and yield tracking connected to the BKS network.

loops.h2: How the Circular Economy of IFS Works
loops.intro: The power of an integrated farm lies in its zero-waste cyclical loops.

items.body: Nutrient-dense bottom silt from the pond is excavated annually to enrich vegetable and crop beds.
Paddy straw, maize stalks, and green fodder grown on field borders feed the cattle and goats.
Cattle manure produces clean biogas for energy, while residual bio-slurry fertilizes the vegetable patches and enhances pond plankton.
Surplus vegetable leaves, azolla culture, and kitchen greens directly supplement fish and poultry feed.

loops.footnote: Illustrative, model-based: a well-run closed loop can reduce bought-in farm costs while lifting output. The 50% to 70% range is not a guarantee. Outcomes vary by farm size, location, management, crop mix, input costs, yields and market conditions.

impact.h2: Economic & Social Impact for Bengal Farmers
impact.caveat: Figures below are illustrative, model-based potential. Actual outcomes vary by farm size, location, management, crop mix, input costs and market conditions.

items.title: 365-day cash flow (illustrative model)
items.body: Daily income from milk and eggs, weekly income from fresh vegetables and green herbs, monthly income from fish harvest, and seasonal income from grain/fruit harvests.

items.title: 3× to 5× income range (illustrative model)
items.body: A marginal farmer earning ₹40,000 to ₹60,000 annually under single-crop paddy can generate ₹2,00,000 to ₹3,50,000+ net profit per acre per year under a well-managed IFS.

items.title: Climate Resilience
items.body: Even if heavy unseasonal rains damage a standing field crop, the aquaculture, dairy, fruit trees, and poultry units continue generating income unhindered.

items.title: Youth Re-engagement
items.body: Transforming farming into a multi-enterprise, tech-enabled micro-business stops distress migration and attracts rural youth to stay and build local enterprises.

viz.h2: How the pieces feed each other
viz.intro: The ring reads clockwise. The list under it names each transfer. Tap a card to highlight what it feeds next.
viz.summary: Residue feeds livestock and compost. Manure and compost return to soil. Pond and field water support fish, duck and horticulture. Produce moves to market. Income returns to the household.

nodes.title: Crop
nodes.body: Cereals, pulses, oilseeds and fodder. Residue is feed or compost.

nodes.title: Horticulture
nodes.body: Vegetables, fruit and homestead trees on the same holding.

nodes.title: Livestock
nodes.body: Dairy, poultry, duckery. Dung and leftover feed return to soil.

nodes.title: Fishery
nodes.body: Ponds and rice–fish. Pond silt returns to fields.

nodes.title: Bee, mushroom
nodes.body: Allied livelihoods on the same holding.

nodes.title: Compost
nodes.body: Crop residue, dung and pond silt as compost.

nodes.title: Soil
nodes.body: Organic return keeps the loop closed.

nodes.title: Water
nodes.body: Field, pond and homestead water planned together.

nodes.title: Market
nodes.body: Produce, milk, eggs, fish and fruit toward local markets and FPOs.

nodes.title: Household
nodes.body: Daily, monthly and seasonal cash on the same land.

prototype.h2: The East Kolkata Wetland Prototype & 5,000 Village Scale-Up
prototype.status: To prove this model at scale, Bharatiya Krishak Samaj (BKS) is constructing the First Live IFS Demo Farm in the East Kolkata Wetlands, adjacent to Salt Lake Sector V.

items.title: Live Demonstration
items.body: Showcases real-time aquaculture, raised-bund organic horticulture, solar integration, and precision livestock management.

items.title: Durga Puja 2026 Showcase
items.body: Intended as the central live pavilion for Bharatiya Krishak Samaj Pujo 2026, so visitors can see a working farm model. No attendance figure is claimed here.

items.title: Mission 5,000 Farms
items.body: Using this prototype as the operational blueprint, the mobilisation target is about 5,000 farming teams across Bengal’s districts and about 5,000 local integrated model farms between Durga Puja 2026 and 2027. That is a goal, not a completed count.
